kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea remains paused following episode 55 on October 17. The forecast for episode 56 fountaining has been pushed to Nov. 1-7, 2026.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu remains paused following episode 55 fountaining on October 17, 2026. Slow, steady inflation continues at the summit. Based on current deformation trends and assuming magma chamber inflation follows similar patterns to those established during previous episodes, the forecast window for episode 56 fountaining is November 1–7, 2026. Summit Observations: Strong glow was seen from the west vent overnight, with weaker but relatively steady glow from the north vent. The south vent remains dark after being buried during episode 55. Seismic tremor continued yesterday and overnight, with relatively steady background amplitudes interrupted by occasional and periodic stronger pulses. These fluctuations are characteristic of the pauses between fountaining episodes, with pulses typically associated with increased glow and gas emissions. Three earthquakes less than M1.5 were recorded at Kīlauea summit in the last 24 hours. Summit tiltmeters have recorded an overall positive trend since the end of episode 55, with several small, short-term oscillations. The general pattern remains consistent with post-fountaining recovery observed during previous inter-episode pauses, although rate of recovery has varied over time. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) has recorded an increase of approximately 0.4 microradians in the past 24 hours for a total of 14.9 microradians of tilt recovered since the end of episode 55. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rates during inter-episode pauses typically range from 1,000 to 5,000 tonnes per day. Light southwesterly winds are expected to transport volcanic gases north toward Volcano and surrounding communities today. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following episode 55 on October 17, 2026, summit tiltmeters initially recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with a steady upward trend that gradually slowed and was interrupted by several small fluctuations. Tilt has continued to increase gradually over the past 24 hours, following a brief negative trend on October 26. This interruption contributed to shifting the forecast window for episode 56 fountaining to November 1–7, 2026. Given the unusual buildup to episode 55, uncertainty remains as to whether summit deformation will follow a sufficiently consistent pattern to allow for precise forecasting of the next episode. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. The buildup to episode 55 differed substantially from previous episodes, with summit tiltmeters recording positive tilt beyond levels typically observed before fountaining, suggesting continued pressurization of the summit magma chamber. This prolonged buildup was punctuated by extended periods of negative or relatively stable tilt, rather than the more consistent upward trends observed before earlier episodes. Episode 55 was also preceded by 39 days of intermittent lava overflows, the longest period of precursory activity recorded before a fountaining episode in the current eruption. During this interval, several short-lived vents opened within Halemaʻumaʻu, and a shallow dike was emplaced beneath Kaluapele. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Kīlauea's volcano alert level and aviation color code remain at ADVISORY/YELLOW. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
